oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @rerank-oncall — elevated 5xx rate on /api/v1/batch-rerank starting ~11:02 UTC, 10% error rate, alerting SLA. latency spike + increased p95. dashboard: https://grafana.internal/rdw/d/rr1/batch-rerank
Maria G.: On it. Joining #incidents. Quick question — customer-facing errors or internal only?
Devon L.: Customer 400s observed in proxy logs. Looks like some requests are failing with shape errors in downstream reranker consumer./proxy returns 400 to clients when reranker returns unexpected vector sizes.
Sanjay K.: Pulling logs from reranker pods now. Running `kubectl logs -lapp=rerank -c reranker --since=30m` — will paste snippets.
Sanjay K.: log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T11:03:12Z ERROR reranker serve: invalid vector shape: expected=512 got=384 request_id=abcd1234
2026-03-15T11:03:12Z WARN  embedder: produced vector_len=384 for model=open-embed-small v2
2026-03-15T11:03:13Z ERROR pipeline: downstream failed: shape-mismatch -> returning 500 to proxy
```
Maria G.: That looks bad — embedding producer is emitting 384-length vectors intermittently. We recently rolled a bake with quantization profile Q4_384 for some smaller models. Could be a variant slipped into the batch pool.
Lucy Ops: Noted customer impact: three customers reported failed batch rerank jobs. CS ticket references are linked in incident doc.
Thomas W.: I'm seeing canary of a new image (rerank:2026.03.14-bake3) started at 10:45 UTC on the batch nodes. Might be the deployment that introduced mixed vector sizes.
Devon L.: For mitigation, can we pin batch workers to the previous image, or evict the new ones? If mixed model variants hit the same batch op, that'll produce shape mismatch.
Maria G.: I'm going to scale down the bake3 replicaSet to 0 on batch nodes and force drain for a quick rollback. Will monitor error rate.
Sanjay K.: Also enabling strict input validation in the proxy as short-term: if vector_len != expected then return soft-fail and route to single-item fallback (slower but safe). Applying patch now.
Maria G.: Executed rollback at 11:18 UTC: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/rerank-batch --to-revision=2026.03.13`
Maria G.: Monitoring... error rate dropping. p50/p95 latency stable.
oncall-bot: Incident severity updated to Sev2 by Maria G.
Devon L.: CS confirmed two failed jobs due to this, both have retry windows — asked them to retry.
Sanjay K.: Saved relevant logs to S3: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1968001123/ — including kube events and embedder logs.
Thomas W.: Hypotheses (quick list):
- H1: New bake image produced an embedder variant (Q4_384) that joined batch pool without version gating -> mixed vector lengths in same batch.
- H2: Router/routing policy allowed multiple model variants to be grouped into same batching worker due to label mismatch.
- H3: Serialization bug in batch endpoint that truncated or padded vectors incorrectly under high load.
Lucy Ops: Marking H1 highest prob based on logs showing produced vector_len=384 tied to bake3 image.
Maria G.: Handoff: I'm offpager at 12:00 UTC. Leaving notes for follow-up RCA. Assigning to @Sanjay K. for deep dive into bake pipeline and routing.
Maria G.: Key artifacts saved: metrics snapshot, kube events, S3 logs, deploy timeline, CS tickets.
Sanjay K.: Taking over. Immediate next steps I will do:
- reproduce locally with bake3 image to confirm vector size behavior
- inspect model config registry for mixup in model tags (embedding.family, vector_len)
- check autoscaler labeling that assigns bake variants to batch pools
- run a small canary job that forces batching to verify shape invariants
Sanjay K.: Preliminary findings: the bake pipeline's manifest for open-embed-small v2 had an incorrect 'vector_len' attribute in the model registry (384 instead of 512). That propagated into bake3 image metadata.
Sanjay K.: Command I used to check registry: `curl -s https://registry.internal/models/open-embed-small-v2 | jq .metadata` -> returned "vector_len": 384
Maria G.: Good catch. That explains why the embedder produced 384. How did the incorrect metadata get into registry? Audit next.
Devon L.: For immediate prevention: lock mixing policy so that batch workers only accept identical vector_len models (strict label match). Small config change proposed.
Lucy Ops: I'll open an ops change PR for label gating + an alert for vector_len variance across pool.
jira-bot: Created INC-4629: "rerank batch vector_len variance causing downstream errors" and linked ticket INC-4629 to this thread.
Sanjay K.: Timeline for RCA:
- Root cause hypothesis confirmed (model registry metadata mismatch) — action: revoke bake3 tag and rebuild with correct vector_len (in progress).
- Impact: three customer jobs failed; internal SLA breach window ~11:02–11:21 UTC; mitigated by rollback at 11:18 UTC.
- Next steps: audit bake manifest generation, add unit test to prevent vector_len mismatch, add gating in batch router, improve canary validation (check metadata vs runtime outputs).
Maria G.: Communication: I'll coordinate a short post to #customer-ops and support with the incident summary, mitigation steps, and when we expect fixes.
Thomas W.: I'll own the router gating PR and run it through canary tomorrow during low traffic.
Lucy Ops: I'll draft the RCA skeleton and timeline entries, will attach logs from S3 and the reproduce notes.
Sanjay K.: Leaving checklist in the ticket: repro steps, logs, PR links, owner assignments. Will hand back to Maria for final review.
Maria G.: Thanks team. :white_check_mark: We'll schedule a 1-hr RCA tomorrow to finalize fixes and assign follow-ups.
Maria G.: Handoff complete — marking thread as archived in #incidents once RCA doc lands.
notes: incident bot thread for reranker pipeline vector length variance; includes mitigation, handoff, log snippets, hypotheses, timeline, and owners
